subject: chemistry
question_text: What is an ionic bond? Which conditions favour its formation? Explain the formation of sodium chloride.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This question comes from the enumeration sweep: the book asks the PROPERTIES of ionic compounds but never the ionic bond's definition, formation or favourable conditions — the section NCERT opens the topic with. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1+2 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Definition
lines: two oppositely charged ions, formed by the
complete transfer of one or more electrons
from a metal atom to a non-metal atom.
steps.why: The two defining phrases are complete transfer (against sharing) and electrostatic attraction (what actually holds the ions), so both must appear.
common_mistakes: Writing sharing of electrons. Sharing is covalent; the ionic bond transfers completely.
Leaving out oppositely charged — like ions repel.
steps.memory_tip: Transfer makes the ions; attraction between them is the bond.
steps.margin_note: Electrovalent bond is the same term — either name is accepted.

steps.label: Favourable conditions
lines: An ionic bond forms easily when:
1. the metal has a low ionisation enthalpy
2. the non-metal has a high negative
3. the lattice enthalpy of the crystal
steps.why: Each condition lowers the energy cost of one stage of the formation: removing the electron, attaching it, and packing the ions into a lattice.
common_mistakes: Writing high ionisation enthalpy for the metal. LOW is favourable — the electron must be removable with little energy.
Forgetting lattice enthalpy, the condition that releases most of the energy.
steps.memory_tip: Little energy to remove, much energy released on gaining, strongly packed — the three conditions in order.
steps.margin_note: Three numbered conditions, one line of reason each.

steps.label: Formation of NaCl
lines: Sodium transfers its single outer electron
to chlorine. Both ions reach an octet.

lines.text: Na⁺ + Cl⁻ → NaCl, held by electrostatic attraction

steps.why: The two half-equations show the transfer and the octets it completes; the final line names the attraction that is the bond itself.
common_mistakes: Writing Na⁺ as (2, 8, 1). After losing the electron it is (2, 8).
Stopping at the two ions. The bond is the ATTRACTION line at the end.
steps.memory_tip: One electron moves left to right; the two brackets then read 2,8 and 2,8,8.
steps.margin_note: Both half-equations with shell counts, then the boxed combination line.

insider_note: Three questions in one, and the sodium chloride half is worth as much as the definition and the conditions together. Plan the page so it is not the part that gets rushed at the end.
